why: Mountain Project tags it Snow with a spring/winter snow approach but describes summer approach as boulder fields; normal season unclear.
Snow gully is early-season and a later-summer report found it bare, but no page I read settles the normal season.
The route text says the descent gully holds a steep snow headwall well into summer and parties routinely want an axe.
The route text calls the approach gully 40-50 degree snow through June of a Jun-Sep window needing axe and crampons; a Sept 2023 report also found a snow-filled gully on Cardinal.
A Wenatchee guide says steep snow may need crampons and axe from late spring through mid-summer and an axe is usually needed in late summer.
The route text says this shaded northwest couloir stays snow-filled and lists axe and crampons.
Text says the north aspect holds snow but sheds it by August-September; no page I read settled it.
Only a 1947 June ascent and early-season reports found snow in the gully; the July onward window is not shown either way.
Approach gullies hold snow into late July but the buttress itself is dry rock; nothing settles it.
Snow patches are described outside high summer and I found no page for this ridge in its Aug-Sep window.
The route text says snow lingers on the false summit well into the season and an axe is carried even when lower slopes are dry; web reports vary by year.
Snow slabs and the icy gully are early season; reports found it firm snow in June and nothing settles July-September.
A July report crossed the summit basin without snow while another advised an axe before early August; normal-season snow is unclear.
Snow clears from the ridge through July and reports of the downclimb do not show snow in the normal window.
The route text says the Bailey Range holds snow late, with snow and ice in shaded gullies even in August; a late-June report found the basin snow-covered.
A 35-40 degree snowfield needs an axe outside late season but whether it persists in the normal season is not shown.
Gully and chute snow lingers into July or August but later normal-season status is not shown.
The 45-50 degree gully snow is described mainly for June and early July of a Jun-Sep window.
Snow gullies are described for winter and spring while the July-August window reads as scree.
